'''Karim Alexander Adiprasito''' (born in 1988) is a German mathematician at the [[Institut de mathématiques de Jussieu – Paris Rive Gauche]] who works in [[combinatorics]]. He completed his PhD in 2013 at [[Free University Berlin]] under the supervision of [[Günter M. Ziegler]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.genealogy.ams.org/id.php?id=174128|title= Karim Adiprasito|work=[[The Mathematics Genealogy Project]] }}</ref> He has held positions at the Hebrew University, and the University of Copenhagen. Since 2022, he is a Directeur de Recherche with the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]], situated at [[Sorbonne University]]. He is of German and Indonesian descent, and bears an Indonesian surname.

He was awarded the 2015 [[European Prize in Combinatorics]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://eurocomb2015.b.uib.no/eurocomb/the-european-prize-in-combinatorics/|title=The European Prize in Combinatorics|work=uib.no|access-date=19 September 2015|archive-date=20 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820150918/http://eurocomb2015.b.uib.no/eurocomb/the-european-prize-in-combinatorics/|url-status=dead}}</ref> for his work in [[discrete geometry]], in particular on realization spaces of [[polytope]]s citing "his wide-ranging and deep contributions to discrete geometry using analytic methods particularly for his solution of old problems of Perles and Shephard (going back to Legendre and Steinitz) on [[projectively unique polytope|projectively unique polyhedra]]."

In joint work with [[June Huh]] and [[Eric Katz]], he resolved the [[Heron–Rota–Welsh conjecture]] on the [[log-concavity]] of the [[characteristic polynomial of matroids]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gilkalai.wordpress.com/2015/08/14/updates-and-plans-iii/|title=Combinatorics and more|author=[[Gil Kalai|Kalai, Gil]] |date=14 August 2015}}</ref>
With Huh, he is one of five winners of the 2019 New Horizons Prize for Early-Career Achievement in Mathematics, associated with the [[Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://blogs.ams.org/beyondreviews/2018/10/18/break-on-through/|title=Break on Through|work=Beyond Reviews: Inside [[MathSciNet]]|first=Edward|last=Dunne|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|date=20 October 2018}}</ref>

Using [[Mikhail Leonidovich Gromov|Mikhail Gromov]]'s work on spaces of bounded curvature, in joint work with [[Bruno Benedetti]] he resolved the [[Hirsch conjecture]] for flag triangulations of [[manifold]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Adiprasito|first1=Karim A.|last2=Benedetti|first2=Bruno|date=2014|title=The Hirsch Conjecture Holds for Normal Flag Complexes|journal=[[Mathematics of Operations Research]]|volume=39|issue=4|pages=1340–1348|doi=10.1287/moor.2014.0661|issn=0364-765X|arxiv=1303.3598|s2cid=1586147}}</ref>

In December 2018, he [[mathematical proof|proved]] [[Peter McMullen]]'s [[Simplicial sphere|g-conjecture]] for simplicial spheres.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gilkalai.wordpress.com/2018/12/25/amazing-karim-adiprasito-proved-the-g-conjecture-for-spheres/|title=Amazing: Karim Adiprasito proved the g-conjecture for spheres!|last=Kalai|first=Gil |authorlink=Gil Kalai|date=25 December 2018|website=Combinatorics and more|language=en|access-date=2019-01-27}}</ref><ref>{{Cite arXiv|last=Adiprasito|first=Karim|date=26 December 2018|title=Combinatorial Lefschetz theorems beyond positivity|class=math.CO|eprint=1812.10454|language=en}}</ref> For his work, he won the 2020 EMS Prize of the [[European Mathematical Society]].
